decision.summary: The screened region (485–492) contains an abrupt multi-sample anomaly centered at index 487, where N, E, and U show extreme, non-physical excursions (e.g., E jumps to +13.13, U to -18.67), inconsistent with a coherent temporary offset. The values at idx 487 appear spurious (likely data glitch or outlier), as surrounding samples (485–486, 490–492) show no sustained displacement nor monotonic return. No confirmed temporary offset interval can be established due to lack of consistent onset, sustained interior, and opposing return across axes.

intervals.observation: N drops sharply from -0.084 (idx 485) to -2.505 (idx 486), then to -11.334 (idx 487); E drops from -0.618 (idx 485) to -1.856 (idx 486), then jumps to +13.128 (idx 487), suggesting a likely outlier or data glitch rather than coherent offset; U drops from -2.180 (idx 485) to -1.350 (idx 486), then to -18.667 (idx 487). The extreme values at idx 487 are inconsistent with sustained motion and lack recovery pattern—return not observed before idx 490, where N/E/U resume near pre-drop levels but with noise. No clear opposing return on any axis; interior not sustained coherently across axes.
